activities.desc: Depart from Pittsburgh (PIT) or Morgantown (MGW). EDT +6h = CEST
Munch's The Scream, Viking gold, and Norwegian art. Indoor, central, jet-lag-friendly
Karl Johans gate, Royal Palace, Akershus Fortress
Walk the sloping marble roof for iconic city + fjord views
200+ granite/bronze sculptures in Frogner Park. Open air, perfect for jet lag recovery
Waterfront dining and bars. Try Amundsen Bryggeri craft beer or Himkok for aquavit cocktails

groupNotes: Keep Day 1 light. National Museum and Vigeland Park are easy-paced. Dinner at Aker Brygge.

lodging.name: Citybox Oslo
lodging.pros: Self-check-in 24/7, central near Oslo Central Station, modern minimalist, free Wi-Fi
lodging.cons: No breakfast, no housekeeping, small rooms

lodging.name: Radisson RED Oslo
lodging.pros: Modern Scandinavian design, excellent breakfast bar, great location near Opera House
lodging.cons: Standard chain feel, no pool, can be noisy

lodging.name: Grand Hotel Oslo
lodging.pros: Historic 1874 Nobel venue, rooftop terrace, exceptional breakfast, prime Karl Johans gate
lodging.cons: Very expensive, dated rooms, no parking

meals.breakfast: Baker Hansen at Oslo Central Station or hotel buffet
meals.lunch: Mathallen Oslo food hall (Vulkan) - seafood soup at Vulkanfisk. Grab extra snacks for the road tomorrow
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schrøder - classic Norwegian home-cooking since 1910. Order fårikål or kjøttkaker with lingonberry. Nightcap at Grand Hotel rooftop bar

directions: Take E18 south from Oslo toward Drammen (45 min, 55 km)
Follow E134 west through Kongsberg and over the mountains toward Haukeli (1.5 hr, 130 km)
Turn onto Rv9 south through Setesdal valley to Evje (1 hr, 95 km)

stops.name: Kongsberg Silver Mines
stops.desc: Historic silver mines dating to 1623. Guided underground tour

stops.name: Setesdal Museum (Rygnestadtunet)
stops.desc: Open-air museum with historic Setesdal farm buildings

stops.name: Evje og Hornnes Geopark
stops.desc: Mineral park with thulite deposits (Norway's national gem)

stops.name: Setesdal valley viewpoint
stops.desc: Scenic viewpoint over the Setesdal valley

activities.desc: E134 west through mountain scenery, then Rv9 south through the beautiful Setesdal valley

activities.text: TrollAktiv family rafting on Otra River
activities.desc: Class 2-3 rapids on Norway's longest river. Family-friendly, guide included, wetsuit provided. Min height 120cm
Historic farm buildings from the 1600s with traditional Setesdal costumes
Self-guided walk through the geopark. Thulite found here

groupNotes: Scenic drive through Kongsberg and the Setesdal valley. TrollAktiv family rafting on the Otra River is the highlight. Evje Hotel is the main lodging option.

lodging.name: Evje Camping & Cabins
lodging.pros: Self-catering cabins, riverside setting, kitchenette, playground
lodging.cons: Shared bathrooms in some cabins, basic, 15-min walk from center

lodging.name: Evje Hotel
lodging.pros: Central location, restaurant on-site, free parking, comfortable modern rooms
lodging.cons: Limited amenities, basic breakfast, small gym

lodging.name: Hovdestøylen Fjellstoge
lodging.pros: Mountain lodge with incredible Setesdal valley views, traditional architecture
lodging.cons: 30 min from Evje, remote, limited dining nearby

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet in Oslo before departing, or Baker Hansen pastries to go
meals.lunch: Café Utsikten in Kongsberg or pack from Kiwi in Oslo
meals.dinner: Evje Hotel restaurant - traditional Setesdal cuisine: spekemat, røykt ørret (smoked trout), homemade flatbread. Walk along the Otra River after dinner

directions: Take Rv9 south from Evje to Rv45 junction (25 min, 32 km)
Follow Rv45 south through Åseral and Bjørnemoen (40 min, 50 km)
Merge onto E39 south toward Stavanger - ferry crossing at Oanes-Lauvvik (55 min, 85 km)

stops.name: Lauvvik-Oanes Ferry
stops.desc: Scenic ferry across Høgsfjorden. Free with AutoPASS

stops.name: Månafossen Waterfall
stops.desc: 92m waterfall with short 1km hike from parking

stops.name: Sverd i Fjell (Swords in Rock)
stops.desc: Three 10m bronze swords monument at Hafrsfjord

stops.name: Preikestolen hike trailhead
stops.desc: Trailhead for Pulpit Rock hike. 604m cliff above Lysefjord

stops.name: Stavanger city center
stops.desc: Explore the city center and harbor area

activities.desc: Scenic drive through Setesdal valley, then E39 south with a fjord ferry crossing
Iconic 604m cliff above Lysefjord. Moderate 8km round trip. Norway's most popular hike
Scenic fjord cruise from Stavanger. See Pulpit Rock from the water
World-renowned craft brewery. Tour includes 6-beer tasting
Cobblestone streets, white wooden houses from the 1800s

groupNotes: Arrive Stavanger ~11am. Afternoon Pulpit Rock hike (depart before 1pm). Evening at Lervig brewery. Families can split: hikers do Pulpit Rock, others explore Old Stavanger.

lodging.name: Comfort Hotel Square
lodging.pros: Modern budget hotel near harbor, breakfast included, free Wi-Fi, central
lodging.cons: Small rooms, basic, no parking

lodging.name: Clarion Hotel Stavanger
lodging.pros: Harbor-side, excellent breakfast buffet, rooftop terrace, modern rooms
lodging.cons: Pricey, compact rooms, parking costs extra

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Maritim
lodging.pros: Harbor views, rooftop terrace with hot tub, excellent seafood restaurant
lodging.cons: Very expensive in peak season, no pool, limited parking

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet in Evje before departing
meals.lunch: Pack from Coop or Kiwi in Evje, or fish soup at Fisketorget in Stavanger
meals.dinner: Lervig Taproom - world-class craft beer with small plates. Try the John John DIPA or barrel-aged stouts. Nightcap at Bølgen & Moi

activities.desc: High-speed RIB boat through Lysefjord past Pulpit Rock and waterfalls
Boulder wedged 984m above Lysefjord. Strenuous 11km hike. Open June-Sept
Tropical garden on Sør-Hidle island. Boat transfer, garden tour, and dinner
Quirky sardine canning history in Old Stavanger
20 min from Stavanger. Scenic wooded course, rated 4.3 on PDGA
Østervåg harbor area, Husfliden for Norwegian crafts

groupNotes: Flex day. Options: challenging Kjeragbolten hike (strenuous), RIB safari, disc golf at Kulleseid, or Flor & Fjære garden trip. Families can split by interest.

lodging.name: Comfort Hotel Square
lodging.pros: Modern budget hotel near harbor, breakfast included, free Wi-Fi, central
lodging.cons: Small rooms, basic, no parking

lodging.name: Clarion Hotel Stavanger
lodging.pros: Harbor-side, excellent breakfast buffet, rooftop terrace, modern rooms
lodging.cons: Pricey, compact rooms, parking costs extra

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Maritim
lodging.pros: Harbor views, rooftop terrace with hot tub, excellent seafood restaurant
lodging.cons: Very expensive in peak season, no pool, limited parking

meals.lunch: Fisketorget (Stavanger Fish Market) - fresh shrimp sandwiches and fish soup
meals.dinner: Tango Bar & Kjøkken - modern Norwegian cuisine. For casual: Eg & Du wood-fired pizzas. Nightcap at Bølgen & Moi

directions: Take E39 north via Byfjord Tunnel (undersea, 5.7 km)
Continue E39 through Haugesund and Åkrafjorden (2 hr, 140 km)
Continue E39 through Sveio and Os to Bergen (1.5 hr, 70 km)

stops.name: Åkrafjorden Scenic Stop
stops.desc: Dramatic fjord with steep cliffs. Langfossen waterfall visible from road

stops.name: Avaldsnes Viking Farm
stops.desc: Reconstructed Viking longhouse with living history demonstrations and animals

stops.name: Langfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: 612m tall waterfall right along E39 near Åkrafjorden

stops.name: Fantoft Stave Church
stops.desc: 12th century reconstructed stave church

stops.name: Bergen city center
stops.desc: Arrive and explore Bergen city center

activities.desc: E39 north with the undersea Byfjord Tunnel, Åkrafjorden views, and ferry crossing
Ferry across Boknafjorden. Part of E39. Free with AutoPASS
612m cascading waterfall right along E39. Quick photo stop
Working Viking farm with longhouse reconstruction and living history
Evening walk up Mount Fløyen. 30-45 min from city center. Panoramic Bergen views

groupNotes: Scenic coastal drive with Åkrafjorden, Langfossen, and Avaldsnes Viking Farm en route. Check into Bergen by late afternoon.

lodging.name: Citybox Bergen
lodging.pros: Modern self-check-in hotel, central near train station, free Wi-Fi, clean
lodging.cons: No breakfast, no staff on-site, small rooms, no parking

lodging.name: Zander K Hotel
lodging.pros: Stylish boutique hotel near Bergen Station, excellent breakfast, rooftop bar
lodging.cons: Small rooms, no parking, rooftop bar can be noisy

lodging.name: Det Hanseatiske Hotel
lodging.pros: Historic hotel inside UNESCO Bryggen building, unique atmosphere, gourmet breakfast
lodging.cons: Very expensive, old building (creaky floors), no elevator to some rooms

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet in Stavanger before departing
meals.lunch: Café at Avaldsnes Viking Farm - pancakes with brown cheese, or Kiwi picnic at Åkrafjorden
meals.dinner: Lysverket - modern Norwegian tasting menu (reindeer, monkfish, cloudberry). Walk up Fløyen for sunset at 11pm

activities.desc: Colorful Hanseatic wooden buildings dating to 1702. Explore alleyways and artisan shops
Panoramic city and fjord views from Mount Fløyen
Fresh seafood on the harbor. Shrimp sandwiches, fish soup, whale meat
Highest Bergen mountain at 643m. Vidden trail to Fløyen (3-4 hr)
12th century reconstructed stave church
Edvard Grieg's home with guided tour and concert hall
Local craft brewery near the Fish Market. Excellent IPAs and stouts

groupNotes: Full Bergen day. Morning: Bryggen and Fish Market. Afternoon: Fløyen funicular + hike or Ulriken cable car. Evening: brewery or Troldhaugen concert.

lodging.name: Citybox Bergen
lodging.pros: Modern self-check-in hotel, central near train station, free Wi-Fi, clean
lodging.cons: No breakfast, no staff on-site, small rooms, no parking

lodging.name: Zander K Hotel
lodging.pros: Stylish boutique hotel near Bergen Station, excellent breakfast, rooftop bar
lodging.cons: Small rooms, no parking, rooftop bar can be noisy

lodging.name: Det Hanseatiske Hotel
lodging.pros: Historic hotel inside UNESCO Bryggen building, unique atmosphere, gourmet breakfast
lodging.cons: Very expensive, old building (creaky floors), no elevator to some rooms

meals.lunch: Bergen Fish Market - ferske reker (fresh shrimp) with bread and mayo, fiskesuppe (fish soup)
meals.dinner: Colonialen - high-end Norwegian gastro. For casual: Pingvinen (affordable Norwegian home-cooking). Nightcap at 7 Fjell Bryggeri taproom

directions: Take E16 east from Bergen through the Arnanipa tunnel (10 min, 12 km)
Continue E16 through Dale and Vaksdal along the fjordside (45 min, 55 km)
Pass through the Stalheimskleiva hairpin bends (steep, narrow, epic views)
Arrive Voss from the east (25 min, 38 km)

stops.name: Tvindefossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Impressive 110m roadside waterfall just south of Voss. Quick photo stop

stops.name: Stalheimskleiva viewpoint
stops.desc: One of Norway's steepest roads with 13 hairpin bends. Panoramic Nærøydalen views

stops.name: Nærøyfjord viewpoint (Gudvangen)
stops.desc: UNESCO fjord panorama. Short detour from main road near Stalheim

stops.name: Voss Gondola
stops.desc: Gondola to 670m with panoramic views

activities.desc: Bergen to Voss via E16. Stalheimskleiva hairpin bend road is spectacular
Outdoor Norway family rafting on Raundal River. Class 2 rapids. Ages 5+
Gondola to 670m with panoramic mountain and fjord views
Alpine trails from gondola top. Blue to Black runs. Bike rental at Bavallen

activities.text: Voss Active High Rope + Zipline Park
activities.desc: 64 treetop elements, 7 ziplines. All ages welcome
More adrenaline on Raundal River. Class 3 rapids. Ages 12+

groupNotes: Morning drive to Voss. Afternoon rafting (Grade 2 family or Grade 3 thrill). Teens will love the zipline park. MTB on gondola-assisted trails. Gondola sunset.

lodging.name: Voss Vandrarheim Hostel
lodging.pros: Budget-friendly, shared kitchen, central, free parking, family rooms
lodging.cons: Hostel-style, shared bathrooms in some rooms, basic breakfast

lodging.name: Park Hotel Vossevangen
lodging.pros: Historic 1880s hotel, lakeside on Lake Vangsvatnet, excellent breakfast, free parking
lodging.cons: Some dated rooms, no AC, average restaurant

lodging.name: Stalheim Hotel
lodging.pros: Perched at top of Stalheimskleiva with jaw-dropping valley views, historic 1885 building, terrace restaurant
lodging.cons: 30 min from Voss, no pool/spa, old building quirks

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet in Bergen before departing
meals.lunch: Tvindefossen Kiosk - pølse i lompe and waffles, or Kiwi in Voss for picnic by Lake Vangsvatnet
meals.dinner: Park Hotel Vossevangen - local trout, lamb, and wild game. After dinner, walk around Lake Vangsvatnet. Nightcap at Voss Microbryggeri

directions: Take E16 east from Voss toward Vinje (15 min, 18 km)
Turn onto Rv13 south through the Granvin tunnel toward Hardangerfjord (30 min, 25 km)
Follow Rv13 along Hardangerfjord through Ulvik and Eidfjord to Kinsarvik (1.25 hr, 82 km)

stops.name: Vøringsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: 182m waterfall in Eidfjord. New staircase bridge and Fossli Hotel viewpoint. Norway's most famous waterfall

stops.name: Steinsdalsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Walk behind the waterfall curtain. 50m tall, roadside near Norheimsund

stops.name: Hardanger Bridge viewpoint
stops.desc: One of Norway's longest suspension bridges (1,310m). Photo stop

stops.name: Hardanger Cider Farm
stops.desc: Visit a local cider farm in Ulvik. Norwegian fruit orchard cider tasting

activities.desc: Rv13 through Granvin and along the Hardangerfjord. Cross the massive Hardanger Bridge
182m waterfall. Walk the new staircase bridge for epic photos. Fossli Hotel cafe
Walk behind the curtain of this 50m waterfall. One of Norway's most accessible
Guided blue ice glacier walk with crampons. Views over Hardangerfjord. Equipment provided
Visit a local cider farm in Ulvik or Lofthus. Norwegian fruit orchard cider
Sunset fjord cruise from Kinsarvik or Lofthus. Fruit orchards on fjord slopes

groupNotes: Scenic drive with Vøringsfossen and Steinsdalsfossen en route. Afternoon: Folgefonna glacier walk or cider tasting at local farms. Evening fjord cruise.

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Vøringfoss
lodging.pros: Modern hotel at Vøringsfossen waterfall, stunning waterfall views, good breakfast
lodging.cons: Limited dining nearby, remote, thin walls

lodging.name: Hotel Ullensvang
lodging.pros: Historic waterfront hotel on Hardangerfjord, stunning fjord views, large outdoor pool, fruit orchard gardens, excellent restaurant
lodging.cons: Very expensive, some dated rooms, large hotel can feel impersonal

lodging.name: Iris at Salmon Eye
lodging.pros: Michelin-starred floating restaurant + luxury rooms, most exclusive Hardanger dining
lodging.cons: Extremely expensive, limited availability, no typical amenities

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet in Voss before departing
meals.lunch: Fossli Hotel café at Vøringsfossen - waffles with brunost and coffee with a waterfall view
meals.dinner: Hotel Ullensvang Restaurant - local trout, Hardanger lamb, Telefon cider. Splurge: Iris at Salmon Eye Michelin-starred floating restaurant. Walk the fruit orchards at midnight

activities.desc: Norway's largest national park. Vast arctic plateau with wild reindeer. Trails near Eidfjord
Calm fjord kayaking on Hardangerfjord in Ulvik. Beginner-friendly, equipment included
15km easy paved path along the fjord. Stop at Hardanger Nature Center
Fresh apples, cherries, and cider from roadside fruit stands in Lofthus and Ulvik
Interactive exhibits on Hardangerfjord ecosystem and glacier history
Last night dinner at Hotel Ullensvang. Celebrate the trip overlooking the fjord

groupNotes: Final full day. Options: Hardangervidda plateau hike, Ulvik kayaking, or cider farm visits. Farewell dinner at Hotel Ullensvang.

lodging.name: Thon Hotel Vøringfoss
lodging.pros: Modern hotel at Vøringsfossen waterfall, stunning waterfall views, good breakfast
lodging.cons: Limited dining nearby, remote, thin walls

lodging.name: Hotel Ullensvang
lodging.pros: Historic waterfront hotel on Hardangerfjord, stunning fjord views, large outdoor pool, fruit orchard gardens, excellent restaurant
lodging.cons: Very expensive, some dated rooms, large hotel can feel impersonal

lodging.name: Iris at Salmon Eye
lodging.pros: Michelin-starred floating restaurant + luxury rooms, most exclusive Hardanger dining
lodging.cons: Extremely expensive, limited availability, no typical amenities

meals.lunch: Roadside fruit stand picnic in Lofthus - fresh strawberries, cherries, apples, local cheese. Bread from local bakery
meals.dinner: Hotel Ullensvang Restaurant - farewell dinner with Hardanger trout and grilled lamb. Cloudberries with cream for dessert. Pair with Hardanger cider. One last fjord sunset walk at 11pm

activities.desc: CEST to EDT (-6h). Return to Pittsburgh (PIT) or Morgantown (MGW). Coordinate ahead
Grab a last kanelbolle, walk Bryggen, or visit the Fish Market for souvenirs
Brunost, aquavit, Norwegian wool, Freia chocolate

groupNotes: Departure day from Bergen Airport (BGO). Flytoget or taxi to airport.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet or Baker Hansen at Bergen Station
meals.dinner: On the plane or at home
